assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original visual reference concept for an existing isometric fantasy tower-defense game, PREVIEW ONLY.
Style: clean hand-painted CARTOON 2D environment art, broad rounded painted volumes with restrained warm dark-brown contour lines, muted olive/lime grass, warm wood, pale gray granite, dark charcoal iron, tiny rusty iron accents. Match a cohesive fantasy settlement game with chunky wooden watchtowers, curved terracotta red roof tiles, iron bands and natural painted stone. Not pixel art, photorealism, low-poly render, miniature clay or cinematic concept art.
Camera: fixed orthographic isometric game camera about 55 degrees above ground horizon, visible tops and front faces, no perspective vanishing point, no horizon or sky. Gentle upper-left daylight and soft grounded contact shadows.
Composition: one landscape concept illustration, wide landscape frame, entire irregular resource district and attached production building completely in frame with generous margins. Show the building much smaller than the resource district. The district must read as a substantial traversable-world landmark containing a large resource reserve, not one oversized resource prop. Natural ground blends outward into a simple quiet muted green backdrop, no floating island or cutaway world cube. Crisp silhouettes and readable material separation at game zoom.
Constraints: original artwork for this project. No text, lettering, labels, diagrams, arrows, UI, logos, watermarks, borders, characters, combatants, towers, conveyor networks, industrial factory machinery, extra resource types or fantasy crystals. Scenic reference only, no exact tile count or gameplay claims.
Subject: a LARGE DENSE CONIFER FOREST and a small SAWMILL at its accessible outer edge. Many individually legible varied-height firs in connected irregular clustered groves make an extensive forest; their pointed tiered olive-green crowns and warm grooved trunks echo the project's compact conifer resource. Preserve a scalloped natural forest edge with a few walkable openings; do not make a solid rectangle of tree tops. Keep most of the dense forest behind the sawmill, so it cannot hide the structure.
Sawmill: a small open-sided timber workshop, thick honey-brown beams and iron braces, a curved red tile roof on part of the workshop; a clearly visible large toothed circular saw bench cutting a log, short log stacks, neat cut plank bundles. Its identity must read instantly as lumber production rather than a house or windmill.
Forest renewal: beside the mill show a modest clearly recognizable sapling nursery, rows of small conifer seedlings and a graduated patch of young regrowing firs between a few cut stumps and mature trees. Make forest -> harvested edge -> young regrowth visually understandable through the scenery alone, with no arrows or magical glow.
The forest is the dominant resource landmark; the workshop occupies only a small edge clearing. No river, waterwheel, large fantasy tree or single giant tree.

Subject: an EXTENSIVE PALE GRANITE ROCK MASS with a small QUARRY WORKSHOP at its accessible foot. The dominant landmark is a broad connected natural rocky escarpment, low and wide enough not to hide the playfield, with rounded angular pale warm-gray granite faces, readable coarse cracks, broad stratified ledges and a few grassy seams. Its visual footprint is many times the workshop's; do not depict one giant boulder or one sharply vertical mountain peak.
Worked quarry edge: carve several wide open stepped extraction benches into one side of the rock mass, with a clear contrast between the irregular untouched stone and fresh lighter flat cut faces. Show large partly separated rectangular blocks, a few finished stone blocks and broken stone chips. This is OPEN stone extraction, clearly distinct from an underground mine.
Small production building: heavy stone foundations, honey-brown timber shelter with curved terracotta roof and iron straps, a compact timber lifting crane/derrick over the extraction work area, simple chisel tools and a stone staging pad. The building belongs beside the connected stone deposit; the deposit remains much larger. Keep the foreground open for the player's approach.
No deep black pit, cave entrance, metal vein, orange ore, crystals, kilns, smelters, locomotives or giant mountain blocking most of the composition.

Subject: a substantial DARK IRON-BEARING ROCK DISTRICT with a clearly visible MINE SHAFT CUT DOWN INTO THE GROUND and a compact mine production station on its rim. Dark charcoal and cool slate rock masses with restrained rusty orange iron seams tie the place to the game's established iron outcrop; the rust is a natural mineral surface, not glowing lava or magical light.
Key read: an open stone-hewn downward excavation, an irregular broad oval/squared shaft whose inner rock walls visibly descend through several stepped ledges into a dark lower depth. The fixed elevated camera must see INTO the shaft. A short stone stair/ramp starts at the rim and visibly leads down along one inner wall. It must unmistakably read as mining UNDERGROUND, not a horizontal cave mouth in a cliff and not merely a quarry cut.
Production station: a compact heavy timber headframe standing over one part of the stone-lined shaft, wrought-iron bands, a pulley and rope hoist with an ore bucket, a small adjacent roofed winch house with curved terracotta tiles. A few chunks of gray iron ore with rusty seams and a short ore handling platform signal metal mining. No smelting furnace or glowing molten metal: this is ore extraction, not processing.
The mine is visually embedded in a much larger connected natural rocky deposit with sparse grass around the outskirts. Its broad low enclosing rocks frame the shaft while leaving the opening and approach clearly visible. No vast skyline, giant peak, extensive rail/logistics system, gold, gems, crystals or coal-dominated heaps.
